title: Small Steps Towards Independence: Potty Training Your Child
summary:
Imagine this scene with me: your little one, who was taking their first steps just yesterday, stands before you today with sparkling eyes, asking for your help with something that concerns only them. This might be their desire to use the toilet, or even just their attempt to take off their clothes by themselves. These small moments are major gateways to their independence, and the way you respond to them contributes to building their self-confidence and independence.

Potty training a child is not just about teaching a healthy habit; it's a journey of building self-confidence and self-reliance. It begins when your child shows readiness, which is often between the ages of two and three years. Starting before this readiness can cause unnecessary frustration and pressure, and may delay the process instead of speeding it up. Remember that every child is unique and has their own pace of growth and development, and your role is to observe and support, not to push or force.

Start by teaching them simple, specific steps: how to clean themselves after using the toilet, and you can gradually introduce them to the recommended bathroom etiquettes explained by scholars—such as stepping in with the left foot and exiting with the right—and teach them the authentic supplications for entering and exiting as part of their daily routine, to instill these manners in a loving way. The most important thing is to be a role model for them, and to offer help with gentleness and patience, to encourage them to serve themselves and take on their small responsibilities. This instills in them the seeds of diligence and self-reliance, far from dependency.
try_this: Today: Start by teaching your child one simple step of using the toilet, such as washing hands after using it, or helping them take off their clothes before entering.
